title: Workspace Lambda Self-Hosted Execution v1
goal: Design, validate, and if safety gates pass pilot a project-isolated GitHub Actions execution lane on the existing Lambda workstation so ChatGPT/GitHub-driven software work can execute and validate directly in the real target environment without routine human-terminal mediation, while preserving project authority, minimizing host risk, and keeping existing GitHub-hosted CI as the known-good control.
acceptance_criteria: Current GitHub self-hosted runner capabilities, security guidance, ephemeral/JIT registration options, runner isolation boundaries, artifact/log handling, and billing implications are researched from current primary sources.
The design explicitly distinguishes ordinary GitHub-hosted CI from heavyweight Lambda validation and does not replace the existing known-good CI path merely because a Lambda lane exists.

A threat model identifies risks from AI-generated workflow code, repository compromise, credential leakage, cross-project access, host filesystem access, Docker/root-equivalent access, network reachability, GPU/resource exhaustion, persistence, stale workspaces, and production-state mutation.

Each project receives an isolated execution identity and workspace; a research-engine job cannot read/write PADataset, course repositories, personal SSH credentials, production research data, or another project's runner state unless a separately authorized bridge is declared.
Runner processes do not execute as the normal `atrott` login account and have no sudo access or personal SSH/Git credentials.
A cleanup/reprovision strategy prevents one job's mutable workspace/environment from silently contaminating later jobs while still allowing bounded reusable caches for expensive dependencies/models.
A cache design separates immutable/read-mostly shared model/package caches from per-project mutable environments and records ownership/versioning/invalidations.
A resource-control design covers CPU, RAM, GPU allocation, disk quotas/scratch, concurrency, timeouts, process cleanup, and model-server leak detection.
A secrets model uses least-privilege GitHub tokens/runner registration material and prevents workflow code from gaining broader host or account credentials than required.

The pilot supports a closed loop: ChatGPT mutates an isolated Git branch -> GitHub dispatches Lambda validation -> the runner executes/tests/benchmarks -> logs/checks/artifacts are returned through GitHub -> ChatGPT can inspect evidence and revise/re-run without human SSH.
The first pilot is bounded to research-engine and cannot mutate production scientific state or start sustained daemon work.
The pilot proves both ordinary code validation and one representative GPU/hardware-aware validation path on Lambda.
The design documents how additional repositories such as PADataset can opt in through separate project runner identities and policies rather than sharing one unrestricted runner account.
Existing human-terminal execution remains available as break-glass recovery but is no longer required for routine Lambda validation once the pilot is accepted.
No self-hosted runner is registered as a persistent privileged host service until the threat model, isolation design, and recovery/kill-switch plan are durably accepted.

The executor may enter a waiting state only while external compute is actually in progress or a human-only credential/privilege action is required; once a job reaches a terminal state, its evidence must be consumed immediately and the next safe repair/re-run action must proceed without waiting for the user.

Privileged bootstrap/orchestration code that crosses shell/process boundaries must have executable regression coverage for the exact child-shell control flow; static string assertions and bash -n alone are insufficient acceptance evidence.

P3/P4 runner timeout policy must be expressed as an ordered invariant rather than independent magic values: trusted workflow timeout < systemd runner lifetime < outer launcher watchdog, with executable regression coverage.

P5 acceptance removes routine human SSH/PAT relay while preserving the accepted P2-P4 boundaries: unprivileged network-facing controller credential separation, narrow root provisioner with no GitHub credential, one-job ephemeral project runner, exact trusted workflow authorization, and fail-closed cleanup/evidence.
constraints: Do not modify or disable the existing GitHub-hosted CI implementation during architecture research.

Do not register a self-hosted runner, install a runner service, change host users/groups, expose Docker/root privileges, or alter production Lambda state until the safety architecture reaches an explicit implementation gate.
Do not use ChatGPT Work or paid cloud compute as the primary execution surface.
Treat the Lambda workstation as valuable multi-project infrastructure, not a disposable CI VM.
Do not grant the runner access to the normal user's SSH keys, shell history, browser credentials, personal home contents, or unrelated repositories.
Do not add the runner identity to the Docker group merely for convenience; Docker-socket access is root-equivalent and requires an explicitly reviewed isolation design if ever used.
Prefer repository-scoped runners or equivalently strong project-level authorization boundaries for the initial pilot.
Prefer ephemeral/per-job runner semantics or explicit post-job destruction/cleanup where technically feasible; persistent mutable runners require stronger contamination controls.
Heavyweight model caches may be shared only if mounted read-only or governed by a cache-specific owner/policy; jobs must not be able to corrupt another project's cache or production model state.
No workflow originating from an untrusted fork/public contribution may execute on the Lambda pilot.
Production databases, daemon services, and scientific materialization paths are denied by default for CI jobs; explicit acceptance workflows may receive narrower capabilities later.
Preserve the current EXTRACT redesign state and its PR/CI progress; this infrastructure task is a sibling/child capability project, not a replacement.

Do not idle after a CI/runner job has reached a terminal state. Immediately inspect the result/artifacts, heartbeat the state transition, and continue the bounded fix/re-run loop unless blocked by a human-only credential or privilege boundary.

Do not embed multi-line child-shell programs in bash -c/ceu single-quoted strings in privileged bootstrap code; use quoted stdin heredocs or a non-shell orchestration language, and execute representative child-shell blocks in CI.

evidence: Current GitHub connector can mutate branches/PRs, create PR conversation comments, inspect workflow runs/jobs, list/download workflow artifacts, and rerun jobs.
This is sufficient for ChatGPT -> GitHub trigger -> Lambda execution -> GitHub evidence -> ChatGPT revision without routine human SSH once the runner foundation exists.
GitHub, GitLab, and Buildkite converge on ephemeral/single-job workers, clean workspaces, scoped credentials, network segmentation, and compartmentalized runner responsibilities.

GitHub's official actions/scaleset Runner Scale Set Client supports custom autoscaling outside Kubernetes, JIT configs, message sessions, and ephemeral runners by default; it is Public Preview, so the implementation must pin an exact version/commit behind a local adapter.
GitHub pwn-request guidance supports keeping the trusted Lambda workflow on the default branch and treating candidate PR source as untrusted data with no secrets/write token.
systemd/cgroup-v2 controls on Ubuntu 22.04 support the selected native filesystem/process/resource/device/network sandbox family.
NVIDIA CDI/rootless container support is credible second-stage hardening but is not required for the native systemd pilot.
Replaced hand-rolled GitHub queue/JIT polling with a pinned official Runner Scale Set Client.

Split the network-facing GitHub listener (ci-controller, unprivileged, repo-scoped App/PAT) from a tiny root provisioner that has no GitHub credentials and accepts only root-manifest-allow-listed project/profile/JIT requests.
Changed persistent cache policy from project-writable to trusted-write/read-only-to-candidate-jobs; candidate downloads/build cache remain ephemeral staging.
Retained per-project Unix identities, fresh one-job runner workspaces, no Docker socket, no sudo, no personal credentials, and current GitHub-hosted CI as rollback/control.
Historical result label PASS_WITH_FOLLOWUPS normalized to PASS for current v2 schema; the original nuance remains in this evidence and later validation entries.
Probe confirms Ubuntu 22.04.5, kernel 6.8, systemd 249, unified cgroup v2, 32 logical CPUs, ~270 GB RAM, and dual RTX A4500 20,470 MiB GPUs.
ci-research-engine does not yet exist and /home/atrott is 0750, supporting dedicated-UID isolation if the new UID receives no atrott group membership.
NVIDIA character devices are currently broadly writable, proving GPU assignment must use a real device/cgroup boundary rather than CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES alone.
Production PostgreSQL listens on wildcard IPv4/IPv6 and Tailscale/local services exist, proving network denial is mandatory.

Follow-ups before host mutation: correct /srv filesystem/quota probe, locate PostgreSQL bindir, inspect firewall/nft state, and positively test systemd device/network restrictions with non-runner transient probes.
